Application Materials.content:
For Masters applicants, supporting documents include:
- **A transcript**: “We will need a transcript (in English or a certified translation) giving full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained.” Applicants should send scanned or certified copies of transcripts and **not** originals during the admissions process.
- **English language proficiency results**: applicants who are not nationals of a [majority English-speaking country](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/) need to submit evidence of English proficiency.
- **One completed reference**: applicants should check whether one or two references are required for the programme. At least one reference should normally be from an academic referee able to comment on academic work and suitability for postgraduate study; where this is not possible, references from other sources such as an employer or colleague may be accepted. References from family members, partners or spouses cannot be accepted.
- References can be uploaded via the online application system, via the Gateway after applying, posted, sent through the [enquiry form](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/enquiry/), or emailed by the referee from a university or company email address. Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company official stamp, or provided on official institution/company letterhead.
- References for Postgraduate applications must be in **pdf format, on headed paper, dated, signed/stamped and recommend you for your chosen programme**. If sent directly by the referee, they should come from the referee’s institutional or company email address and be sent to [pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk), with the student reference number, name and programme of study.
- **Personal statement**: “not all programmes require one,” but applicants may provide one. Exeter advises tailoring it to the course, explaining how the course links past and future study/career plans, showing abilities and fit with the course, giving evidence of skills, commitment and enthusiasm, explaining reasons for studying at Exeter, and describing particular interest in the subject. The personal statement should **stick to under 500 words**, use short clear sentences, may use headings, should be proofread, and should use a standard font such as Arial or Times New Roman, text size 11.
For an initial decision on taught programme applications, applicants should send as many required supporting documents as possible with the application. As a **minimum**, they must complete the Module Information section of the application form with details of outstanding modules and expected completion date, and send any interim transcripts available to support the application. International students do not need to provide original copies at the application stage and are advised not to send them during the application process.

Application Deadlines.content: Teaching starts for most programmes in late September. For **international applicants** wishing to join in 2026/2027, the application deadline is **23:59 Friday 11 September 2026** UK time. Applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as possible; international applicants are advised to submit a complete application by **mid-July** for September start.

Academic Requirements.content:
- General entry requirement: **A 2:2 degree with honours**.
- For applicants from China: applicants for Exeter master's courses must obtain a bachelor's degree certificate and graduation certificate from a domestic university recognized by the Chinese Ministry of Education, and achieve results equivalent to a UK **2:1 or 2:2**; different courses have different grade requirements, so refer to the official master's course page.
- For 2026 entry postgraduate taught applicants from China, the China equivalent for a UK **2:2** requirement is **70%**.
- For China: Exeter has cancelled the previous requirement based on domestic university ranking; all Chinese universities are assessed using a unified score standard, and all undergraduate institutions on the official Chinese Ministry of Education recognized list are accepted.
- For China: some courses may have additional undergraduate subject-background requirements.

Program Overview.content:
Duration: 1 year full time. Campus: Streatham Campus.
- The MSc Marketing and Business Analytics course dives deeper into the analytical side of marketing while providing a strong foundation of core marketing skills.
- The programme develops skills at the intersection of marketing, programming, and analytics for making data-driven marketing decisions.
- Students gain expertise in marketing and analytics through marketing strategy, digital marketing planning, applied digital analytics, programming for business analytics and hands-on projects with real businesses. The course explores Statistics, AI, Data-based technologies and Consumer behaviour.
- Students learn through real-world applications, industry partnerships and digital analytics tools to tackle contemporary marketing challenges.
- Students learn from expert academics and industry guest speakers while joining a diverse, international student community and active business societies.
- Students can choose a business project or marketing project option to align the degree with career goals.
- High achieving students have the opportunity to apply for the Quantitative Techniques for Economics and Management (QTEM) programme, which includes an internship and semester abroad.
Top 10 in the UK for Business graduate prospects, Complete University Guide 2025. Triple accredited Business School: AMBA, AACSB, EQUIS. Top 10 in the UK for Business, Management and Marketing: 9th in The Times and The Sunday Times Good University Guide 2025 and [8th in the Complete University Guide 2027](https://www.thecompleteuniversityguide.co.uk/league-tables/rankings/business-and-management-studies). 1st in the UK for Marketing graduate prospects, [The Complete University Guide 2027](https://www.thecompleteuniversityguide.co.uk/league-tables/rankings/marketing?sortby=graduate-prospects).
The MSc Marketing and Business Analytics programme is accredited by the Chartered Institute of Marketing (CIM). Students who choose the marketing project pathway and achieve an overall Pass grade or higher on this programme receive exemptions towards the CIM’s Professional and Digital Marketing qualifications (Level 3 Foundation Certificate; Level 4 Certificate; or Level 6 Diploma). To achieve the full CIM qualification, graduates must enrol in CIM’s study programme, evidence their degree award, and pass the remaining CIM units within five years of graduation.
The MSc Marketing and Business Analytics offers a dynamic curriculum that blends core marketing theory with advanced analytical techniques. By developing the ability to collect, analyse and interpret data from various sources, students are empowered to make informed, data-driven marketing decisions that drive business growth and success. The course fosters transferable skills such as analysis, problem-solving and resilience, and modules introduce the latest technologies shaping the industry. In the final term, students can tailor their learning through two pathways: a consulting project working with real businesses on live marketing challenges, or a business project focused on business analytics applications. Both options allow students to apply classroom knowledge to real-world contexts, building practical experience highly valued by employers. The course ensures a balance of theory and practice, preparing students to bridge creative marketing strategy with the analytical precision demanded in today’s marketplace.
The programme is delivered through a mix of lectures, seminars, tutorials, industrial presentations, case studies, industry visits, computer simulations, project work and a dissertation. Students develop transferable skills such as management and communication skills, computational techniques, data handling and analysis, problem solving, decision making and research methodology, many addressed within an industrial and commercial context.
Students are allocated a Personal Tutor who is available for advice and support throughout their studies, along with support and mentoring from graduates who are now in industry. There is also a Postgraduate Tutor available to help with further guidance and advice.
Students are taught by experts active in research and practice, discuss the latest ideas, research discoveries and new technologies in seminars and in the field, and become actively involved in a research project. Academic staff are active in internationally-recognised scientific research across a wide range of topics, and students are also taught by leading industry practitioners.
Nataliia Pysarenko is Programme Director for the MSc Marketing and Business Analytics and Senior Lecturer in Marketing at the University of Exeter Business School. Winner of the Woman in Marketing Global Award (Science, 2024), she brings 25 years’ experience in corporate consulting, executive education, research, and mentoring. Nataliia has taught across undergraduate, postgraduate, Executive MBA, and CIM programmes, designing modules in strategy, brand management, and digital marketing. She is also a CIM Fellow and Visiting Professor at the International Institute of Business, Ukraine. [View staff profile](https://experts.exeter.ac.uk/41449-nataliia-pysarenko).
Graduates of marketing and business analytics are in high demand for roles that combine creative marketing insight with analytical and programming language expertise. The MSc in Marketing and Business Analytics gives students the ability to collect and analyse data from different sources, applying statistics, analytical tools, and programming languages to find valuable insights and recommend data-driven marketing strategy and tactics. Pathways include Marketing Analyst, Digital Marketing Analyst, Customer Insights Specialist, Marketing Data Analyst, Data-Driven Brand Manager, Content Analyst, and Data-driven Marketing Manager. As part of the Russell Group, Exeter is ranked among the UK’s top 10 most targeted universities by leading employers, ensuring strong career prospects. Supported by the award-winning careers service and global alumni network, students are equipped to thrive in today’s data-driven business landscape.
After the first year of studies at Exeter, students can progress onto the [QTEM Programme](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroad/pgstudyabroad/qtem/). QTEM aims to prepare students with excellent quantitative and analytical skills to support their future careers as decision makers leading the global business environment. If accepted onto the QTEM Programme, students spend an additional semester studying at one of the prestigious academic partners, followed by a quantitatively focussed internship and participation in the [QTEM Data Challenge](https://www.qtem.org/en/students/data-challenge/1), which includes online data science and leadership courses as well real data analysis. Students are selected and nominated to QTEM by the University of Exeter Business School following a competitive internal application process. Places are limited. The QTEM Programme is open to high achieving students enrolled in selected University of Exeter Business School programmes, including [MSc Marketing and Business Analytics](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/msc-marketing-and-business-analytics/).

Cost of Attendance.content:
For international students, the University estimates a single student living in Exeter or Cornwall will need approximately **£1,300-£2,000 a month** to meet basic living expenses such as accommodation (rent), transport, food and drink, entertainment, utility bills, clothes and socialising.
| Expense | Average cost per week* |
| --- | --- |
| Student halls (bills included) | £150-£270 (self-catered); £250-£345 (catered) |
| Rooms in private accommodation (without bills) | £135-£250 |
| Household bills (gas, electricity, water, broadband & a TV licence) | £30 |
| Groceries | £60 |
| Socialising (dining out, going to cafes & bars) | £40 |
| Public transport | £18 |
| Mobile phone bill (SIM only plan) | £4.50 |
| Student gym membership | £15 |
| **Total** | **£316 - £421/week estimate** |
*Based on average local spend April 2026.
As an approximate estimate for a single person living in shared accommodation, household bills per month are: gas £55 - £75, electricity £65-£85, internet £25 - £35, water £30-£40. A TV Licence costs £13.25 per month.

Financial Aid.content:
The University of Exeter offers scholarships for Postgraduate Taught students, including competitive and merit-based awards, bursaries, and funding advice. Scholarships are payments to support education, awarded on merit, personal achievement and academic ability; bursaries are non-competitive payments intended to help students from disadvantaged backgrounds or those having difficulties funding their studies.
- International students: The University of Exeter has more than **£7 million** in scholarships available for international fee paying students applying to study in **2026/27**, including [Exeter Excellence Scholarships](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/funding/award/?id=5613). A full list is available at [scholarships for international students](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/international-students/funding-scholarships/).
- Class of 2026 scholarships: University of Exeter students graduating in Summer 2026 and progressing direct to a standalone postgraduate programme in 2026/27 can receive a [University of Exeter Class of 2026 Progression Scholarship](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/funding/award/?id=5610) towards tuition fees.
- Alumni scholarships: University of Exeter alumni beginning a standalone postgraduate programme can receive a [University of Exeter Alumni Scholarship](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/funding/award/?id=5609) towards tuition fees. Awards are available to all home and international University of Exeter alumni who meet the stated alumni criteria.
- Alumni Family and Friends Discount: University of Exeter Alumni can refer family members or friends who apply to start an eligible postgraduate programme of study for a **20% discount on their first-year tuition fees** when they enrol.
- Sport scholarships: The [University of Exeter Sports Scholarship Scheme](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/funding/sports-scholarships/) provides a comprehensive support package tailored to each individual athlete.
- Choral scholarships: Exeter Cathedral and three local churches offer scholarship schemes; award values vary depending on weekly duties.
- Aziz Foundation scholarships: The Scholarships Programme offers **100% tuition fee Masters scholarships** to support British Muslims to study at UK universities. Further terms and conditions apply via the [Aziz Foundation website](https://www.azizfoundation.org.uk/scholarships-application/).
- A full list of open scholarships available to postgraduate taught students is available through the University’s funding database: [Search our funding database](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/funding/search/).

Multiple Applications.content: No. When you accept your place on a programme you are committing to that specific programme. Any other offers you may be holding will be released.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Requests for deferral will be considered on a case by case basis. Applicants wishing to defer will need to put their request in writing and [submit it via our enquiry form](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/enquiry/) (please ensure you quote your Exeter Reference Number – which can be found on the top of your original offer email). We aim to notify applicants of an outcome within **10 working days**.
Applicants are only permitted to **defer entry once**. Subsequent to this, a new application will be required which will be considered in line with others applying for entry in that year.
| Start date | Deadline |
| --- | --- |
| Programmes commencing in September | **30 September** |
| All other start dates | **Within 4 weeks of the start date of your programme** |
Applicants who do not request a deferral within this timeframe will be required to reapply, as your original application and documentation will not be retained.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet satisfied academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of offer conditions and how to satisfy these requirements, including [paying your deposit](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/fees/tuition-fee-deposit/), will be given in the offer letter.
- For a **full-time taught postgraduate programme**, applicants need to pay the deposit to secure their place and should pay by the deadline even if they have not yet met all the conditions of the offer.
- The deadline for meeting all conditions is normally **31 August** for September entry. Applicants must supply documentation showing that they have met outstanding academic requirements, English language and/or references, or inform the University by **31 August** what conditions remain and when they expect to meet them.
- If the University does not hear from an applicant by **31 August** and outstanding conditions remain, it reserves the right to either **withdraw or defer the application to the following year**.
- To receive a formal unconditional offer letter and, where needed, a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies, applicants must meet: academic conditions by providing degree certificates, transcripts and references as explained in the Conditional offer letter; non-academic conditions such as a [DBS](http://www.exeter.ac.uk/dbs/) check; and the required standard of English language competence by providing an English language test certificate meeting the [English language requirements](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/).
- Offer holders who successfully complete a [Pre-Sessional English course at the University of Exeter International Study Centre](https://www.exeterisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english) and meet the requirements for progression to their chosen degree are not required to undertake an additional IELTS or TOEFL test. The University does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other INTO centres or organisations.
